title: Snap-On
description: One word, LINTEL, in a heavy sans drawn from straight stems and slabs. Tap a stem near its foot or its head and a square slab serif slides in from the side and seats with a dry click; tap the end of an arm and it takes a beak. Drag along the baseline and an underline runs out under the letters, catching at each letter's edge and tying them into one piece; drag above the caps for an overbar. Double-tap any fitting to knock it off. Every fitting is filled with the letters as one shape, so a seated serif is part of the letter, not a sticker on it.
intent: Matthew Carter's Walker (1995, Walker Art Center), a sans shipped with modular snap-on serifs, underlines and overbars that designers attach letter by letter (https://walkerart.org/magazine/flat-files-6-experimental-posters). Make the attaching itself the piece: a machined fitting that slides in and seats, and bars that link letters.
